title: Prepare NavigationServer for `process()` and `physics_process()` split
body:
Prepares the NavigationServer API for a split of its functionality between frame `process()` and stepped `physics_process()`.

Right now the NavigationServer syncs everything with each physic process step.

Only the RVO avoidance is a stepped process that actually requires physics process steps. This current dependency on physics causes a number of issues for all kinds of other things.

Main motivation and reasoning to split physics process and process:
- Lots of delay and unexpected sync behavior for users when running with physics process for stuff that has zero dependency or relation with physics or a stepped process.
E.g. navigation map, navmesh syncs, path queries, ... they all have nothing to do with physics or a stepped process. The common user expectation is that they should always update as soon as possible and performance feasible instead of waiting x-frames until physics decides to finally do something.
Some users with a low physics tick in their project need to await the sync in their scripts a random x-times until even a NavigationServer update finally happens. Explaining that physics mess to new users over and over is frustrating.
- Lots of opportunities to trigger a performance physics death spiral due the costly updates of the NavigationServer in situations where physics already is trying to play step catchup.
Most updates of the NavigationServer have no benefit for being done more than once in a loop per main iteration frame. It is all wasted performance when run in a physics iteration loop that does between 0 to 8 steps per frame.
- In case of rendering debug with the server the rendered visuals all stutter and are unresponsive when the server only has physics process for its update available. So we need the frame process available through the server api anyway soon™.

I didn't want to cramp all the server changes into the same PR so the newer process() function is only a stub function in this PR for now. I have a few development branches that alread work with this split and git makes a rebase mess everytime for me so it would be good to have that change in already.
